membership.reference: MSC 2026-06-19 comp.tsv, sys.tsv and notes.tsv; Schmutz et al. 2026 (preprint)
membership.scope: Gamma2 Velorum is the confirmed WC8 + O7.5III-V 78.5-day binary. Preserve the MSC convention Aa=WR, Ab=O; retain the existing bright-regor / hip-39953 identity on the WR component. Gamma1 Velorum is the separate Ba/Bb spectroscopic pair. C is the MSC Cphr common-parallax/photometry/RV companion.
membership.repair: The uncertain Aab-Ac link disconnects the confirmed Aa-Ab subtree from A-B in automatic MSC traversal. Two outer relationships also reuse parent t, hiding C. Select only the exact confirmed source branches; do not accept the uncertain Ac source.
membership.excluded: Ac (Cp?; uncertain association), D/E (no reviewed physical membership), and the reportedly spurious WSI 55 visual Ba/Bb detections. Retain the independently measured 1.4826-day spectroscopic Ba/Bb solution, without visual geometry.

retainedUnresolvedMscPhotometry.source: MSC 2026-06-19 comp.tsv A and sys.tsv Aa/Ab
retainedUnresolvedMscPhotometry.scope: Integrated Gamma2 Velorum Aa+Ab flux. Previously shown as Regor A; not a measurement of the WR star alone. Source photometry is retained here and in the frozen MSC rows. The original bright/western catalog measurements, errors and provenance remain in catalog_sources.

bright-regor.source: Schmutz et al. 2026, arXiv:2606.27265v1 (preprint), Table 4 and Section 6.3
bright-regor.scope: Individual Gamma2 Velorum WR component; MSC Aa. Source is the June 2026 preprint, not a refereed journal version.

methods.mass: Relative visual orbit, Kepler system mass and spectroscopic mass ratio at assumed cluster distance 336 +/- 1 pc
methods.radius: O-star Ks flux/model radius; WR radius from optical O/WR radius ratio, not the disputed infrared size

bright-regor.note: Gamma2 Velorum Aa (WR), MSC Aa=WC8: mass 8.3 +/- 0.7 solar masses, model radius R*=3.4 +/- 0.5 solar radii, bolometric luminosity 110000 +/- 40000 solar luminosities. Atmosphere inner-boundary T*=57100 +/- 1700 K is separately retained, not used as photospheric Teff. Withheld individual fields: temperature_k, absolute_mag, metallicity_dex, age_gyr. Schmutz et al. 2026 preprint: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.27265v1. No unresolved Johnson V flux, system radial velocity or minimum mass is assigned to either individual star.

msc-08095-4720-ab.source: Schmutz et al. 2026, arXiv:2606.27265v1 (preprint), Table 4 and Section 6.3
msc-08095-4720-ab.scope: Individual Gamma2 Velorum O component; MSC Ab. Source is the June 2026 preprint, not a refereed journal version.

methods.mass: Relative visual orbit, Kepler system mass and spectroscopic mass ratio at assumed cluster distance 336 +/- 1 pc
methods.radius: O-star Ks flux/model radius; WR radius from optical O/WR radius ratio, not the disputed infrared size

msc-08095-4720-ab.note: Gamma2 Velorum Ab (O7.5III-V): mass 26.4 +/- 0.5 solar masses, radius 13.5 +/- 1.0 solar radii, Teff 35000 +/- 300 K, bolometric luminosity 250000 +/- 40000 solar luminosities. Age 6.9 Myr is a rotational evolutionary-track estimate for the O star (Section 6.4), without a published uncertainty; it is not copied to the WR star. The III-V classification does not select one luminosity class. Withheld individual fields: absolute_mag, metallicity_dex. Schmutz et al. 2026 preprint: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.27265v1. No unresolved Johnson V flux, system radial velocity or minimum mass is assigned to either individual star.

atmosphere_temperature.reference: Schmutz et al. 2026, arXiv:2606.27265v1 (preprint), Table 4 and Section 6.3
atmosphere_temperature.scope: WR inner-boundary atmosphere temperature T*, paired with model radius R*=3.4 +/- 0.5 solar radii. Not a photospheric effective temperature. De Marco et al. 2000 wind-model temperature retained by Schmutz et al. 2026; the discrepant infrared continuum radius (4.2 solar radii) and interferometric emitting-region sizes are not adopted as stellar radii.

axisSource.scope: Published relative axis from the adopted cluster distance, not rescaled with the legacy catalog parallax. The cluster-distance assumption is explicit in Table 4.

orbits.scope: GRAVITY+AMBER relative stellar orbit; omega is published for the WR component (MSC Aa). The app projects secondary Ab relative to primary Aa with the required 180-degree argument conversion. No wide A-B or A-C orbit is inferred. The source reports omega_WR=67.5 and node-line PA Omega=247 degrees. For the app convention (secondary O relative to primary WR, with primary omega converted by 180 degrees), the equivalent projection node is 67 degrees. This normalization reproduces the signed RA/Dec offsets of Table 1; using 247 directly would reverse both stars. Preserve the reported node and argument for display.
